admitted_upstream_claims: LTX-2 is the primary upstream development home replacing legacy LTX-Video.
The observed pipeline surface includes text/image-to-video, distilled generation, IC-LoRA video-to-video, keyframe interpolation, audio-to-video, retake, HDR transformation and lip-dub pipelines.
The observed CLI surface supports CPU and disk offload plus FP8 quantization modes.
LTX-2 multi-GPU inference is single-machine and requires multiple CUDA GPUs with P2P access.
The upstream multi-GPU documentation states that multi-GPU is intended for latency reduction and does not allow a model that cannot fit on one GPU to fit by aggregating VRAM.
LTX-2.3 and earlier LTX-2 releases are subject to the January 5, 2026 LTX-2 Community License Agreement.
LTX-2.5 and future LTX-2.x releases under the newer license are subject to the August 11, 2026 LTX-2.x Community License Agreement.
rejected_or_deferred_claims: Do not represent RTX 3080 plus RTX A1000 VRAM as a combined model-fit pool.
Do not assume custom FP8 kernel support from legacy LTX-Video applies to Ampere or current LTX-2.
Do not place the audio-only t2a pipeline under FA3-VIDEO-001.
Do not claim current LTX-2 video extension support without an observed current pipeline surface.
Do not auto-admit LTX-2.5 or later based on LTX-2.3 license admission.
Do not promote runtime based only on upstream README, static tests, or model availability.
